brief: Use your own system or ClinicBook. You will name your readers, choose the views to provide and write two short decision records.
do: List three readers of your architecture documentation and the three questions each one needs answered.
Choose the views you will provide and say which reader and which question each view serves.
Write a decision record for one important decision with its context, the decision, two alternatives and the consequences.
Write a second record for a decision that was hard to reverse, and note the review date or trigger for revisiting it.
done: Readers: Three readers with three questions each
Views: Each view tied to a reader and question
Decision records: Context, decision, alternatives and consequences
Reversibility: Review trigger recorded for the hard-to-reverse decision
Evidence: The readers and questions, the view list, and two decision records.
experienced: Apply it to a real system your team runs, with real numbers, real owners and real dates.

tips: Set a timer for the step and write a rough first version before you polish. A rough answer is easier to improve than a blank page.
Write for the next person who has to act on this, not for a marker. Use plain words and name things.
Stuck on your own system? Use the sample case in the worked example for this step, then come back to yours.
Prefer numbers, names and dates to adjectives. If you do not know a number, write your best estimate and label it as an estimate.
Save often. Your work stays in this browser only, so download your file at the end of every session.
example:
**Readers:** developer (where does code go? what rules apply? how do I run it?), operator (where does it run? what fails? how do I roll back?), clinic owner (what can it do? what are the risks? what does it cost?).

**Views:** context (owner), building blocks (developer), runtime scenarios (developer, operator), deployment (operator).

**Decision 1.** Context: reminders must arrive at local time in several time zones. Decision: store all times in UTC and convert at the edge. Alternatives: store local time; store both. Consequences: conversion code in two blocks; daylight-saving tests required.

**Decision 2.** Context: choice of database. Decision: one relational database for all blocks, each block owning its tables. Alternatives: separate databases; document store. Consequences: simple operation, harder to split later. Revisit if a second team needs independent deployment.
